recentItems.title: Ed Sheeran addresses tour controversy #EdSheeran
recentItems.description:
Ed Sheeran apologised for "mistakes" and addressed his feelings about the Israel-Palestine conflict at his first concert since the controversy over Macklemore being dropped from his tour and other support acts quitting.

Sheeran said the attacks in Israel on 7 October were "horrific" and what is happening in Gaza is "catastrophic". He said "injustice" in the West Bank also "cannot be overlooked".

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Before the concert in Philadelphia, a protest took place outside the venue where some fans said they could no longer support Sheeran while others hoped politics could stay apart from the music.

Macklemore was forced to leave Sheeran's tour after venue owners threatened to ban him over pro-Palestinian comments on stage, with other acts leaving the tour as well in solidarity.

recentItems.title: 'Women do not feel safe' in South Africa
recentItems.description:
In South Africa, the body of a ninth woman has been found near Johannesburg as people demand action and fears rise over the possibility of a serial killer.

The bodies have been found in the town of Ekurhuleni over the last two months: most of the victims were in their twenties or thirties and some showed signs of sexual assault.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Naeemah Abrahams with the South Africa Medical Research Council says women are fearful and says it is unfair for authorities to tell them to change their behaviour instead of penalising men in a country where gender-based violence has been declared a national disaster.

recentItems.title: Could parents be convicted of child's crimes? #UK
recentItems.description:
Parents could lose welfare benefits or even face prison sentences for crimes committed by their children - as the Government seeks to reform the justice system.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Youth Justice Minister Jake Richards told the Times that parents should be held accountable for their children's behaviour, as well as being far more involved in efforts to turn young offenders away from further crime.

It follows a scathing review into the Southport killings which listed the "catastrophic failures" by Axel Rudakubana's parents to stop the attack.

recentItems.title: Trump’s Greenland deal explained
recentItems.description:
Donald Trump has declared that his security pact with Denmark and Greenland gives the US "permanent control" over the Arctic territory.

Not quite, according to Denmark, which said the agreement would enshrine Greenland's sovereignty and rights to self determination. 

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

While the details of the agreement aren’t known yet, there is a sense that all sides in this deal have claimed victory. 

Donald Trump said this new agreement would grant the US "permanent control over security", while Denmark and Greenland claimed they've protected the territory's sovereignty. 

The US has maintained a military base in Greenland since the Cold War, with the right to deploy forces there. Trump has repeatedly said he wanted to buy the island to the alarm of western allies.

After Greenland was thrust front and centre into geopolitical consciousness, will this agreement finally end the row?

recentItems.title: Benedict Cumberbatch: 'It's good to restore nature' #HowToLiveOnEarth #ClimateChange
recentItems.description:
Oscar-nominated actor Benedict Cumberbatch has plunged into environmental politics with a new feature-length documentary that asks – rather than moving to Mars, how can we continue to live on Earth?

It sets out to investigate how the nature we’re destroying could instead help prevent environmental disaster by humans engaging with it in different ways.

recentItems.title: Scottish activist granted bail after nine years of jail in India
recentItems.description:
A Scottish man has been granted bail, nine years after he was detained in India.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal was arrested in 2017 in connection with alleged terror offences, but has never been convicted.

Scotland's First Minister John Swinney welcomed the news, adding that he hoped Jagtar and his family would be reunited soon, though his legal team warned he is still not a free man.

recentItems.description:

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe] 

Buckingham Palace said yesterday it did not comment on books - but then commented - suggesting Earl Spencer's memories from the time were not correct.
